You probably know your Wi-Fi password. But do you know your water filter model?

Some of the most useful details about your home are the ones you rarely think about. Filter sizes, appliance models, and replacement information can be surprisingly difficult to find when you need them.

I created The Home Systems Record to give those details a place to live: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

Replacing a home filter shouldn't require figuring out the right size all over again.

HVAC filters, refrigerator water filters, and other replaceable parts often have specific model numbers or dimensions. Recording them once can make future purchases easier.

Try making a short replacement reference for your home. Include the item, model or size, last replacement date, and the manufacturer's recommended schedule.

That appliance warranty is much more useful when you can actually find the paperwork.

Purchase dates, receipts, coverage terms, and expiration dates are worth keeping together. Before paying for a repair, you'll have a better starting point for checking whether coverage might apply.

The Home Systems Record includes printable worksheets for organizing important home information: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

A few years from now, "off-white" probably won't be enough information to match your wall paint.

Exact paint codes, brands, finishes, and flooring product names can make future touch-ups or replacements much easier. These details are simple to record when the packaging is still nearby.

Try checking whether you have the exact paint information for your main living spaces. Save the label or write down the product details before they're forgotten.

The easiest time to record a home detail is when it's already in front of you.

Bought an appliance? Save its model number. Replaced a filter? Record the size. Finished a repair? Write down what was done and who handled it. Small habits can gradually build a useful home reference.

The Home Systems Record provides 12 printable worksheets to help organize that information: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

It's funny how the smallest details about a home can become the hardest ones to track down.

A filter model, a paint color, a warranty receipt, or the name of a replacement part might not seem worth recording at the time. But having that information ready can save a frustrating search later.

Homeowners, what's one tiny detail about your house you wish you'd written down when you had the chance?
